subject: Hillside private cluster: sprint-zero node fabric, networking, and encrypted storage plan
messages:

Subject: Hillside - on-prem deployment kickoff: cluster sizing and NIC architecture

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the NDA — excited to get into sprint zero. Attached is a first-pass inventory of our target site (servers + NICs + racks). High-level asks from our infra team:

- Guidance on node-class mix (GPU vs CPU) for inference + small-batch training, and whether we should separate GPU pools by model family.
- Persistent storage recommendations: encryption at rest requirements (customer mandates AES-256), snapshot cadence, and backup/restore expectations.
- Network layout: we currently only have a single external ASN at the colo; would like best practice for VPC/VLAN segregation and egress paths.
- Any constraints for a tenantless/isolated workload model (we need strict tenant boundaries).

Can you share a proposed sprint-zero checklist and a recommended node/storage topology so we can review with our ops team tomorrow?

Attachments: hillside-inventory-20261222.csv (csv)

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
VP Infrastructure, Hillside Analytics

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hillside - on-prem deployment kickoff: cluster sizing and NIC architecture

Alex — thanks, received the inventory. I pulled this into our intake checklist and sketched an initial plan (summary below). I've attached a one-page sprint-zero ops checklist with the items we typically run during preflight.

Summary proposal (high level)
- Cluster topology: 3-control-plane nodes (non-GPU), 2 management-worker nodes for logging/metrics (small CPU), and two GPU node pools: 
  * gpu-large (8x A100-equivalent, 512GB RAM) — inference-heavy models, prefer NUMA-aware placement.
  * gpu-medium (4x A100-equivalent, 256GB RAM) — can be used for smaller models and fallback when large pool is saturated.
- Node isolation: tenantless mode supported by using strict Namespace + NetworkPolicy + dedicated nodeSelectors; we recommend a hardware-dedicated GPU pool per tenant for regulatory workloads.
- Storage:
  * Ephemeral local NVMe for KV-cache (per-GPU node) to reduce token latency.
  * Central encrypted blockstore (CSI LUKS + KMS integration) exposed via StorageClass 'redwood-encrypted-blockstore' with volumeSnapshotClass enabled.
  * Backup cadence: daily incremental snapshots, weekly full snapshots retained for 30 days (we can adapt to your retention policy).
- Networking:
  * VLAN segmentation: management / control-plane / compute / storage / egress.
  * Egress: BGP peering at colo for primary path + failover to secondary provider; recommend an egress gateway with NAT and TLS inspection as required.
  * IP allocation: /23 for compute across racks (example sizing in the attachment).
- Security & compliance: KMS integration for envelope encryption, audit logging at API + infra layers, and optional HSM for key custody.

Open questions for you before we finalize:
1) Do you require hardware HSM for root keys or is cloud KMS acceptable?
2) Are there any constraints on snapshot window (we suggested nightly between 02:00–04:00 local)?
3) Do you have a preferred CSI driver vendor (we can run CSI drivers from the cluster or via NetLayer managed plugin)?

Next steps:
- If this looks good, we'll schedule a 90-min preflight with your ops + NetLayer next week.
- Jonas will follow up with detailed storage class choices and PV sizing.

Attachments: redwood-sprintzero-ops-checklist-20261223.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hillside - on-prem deployment kickoff: cluster sizing and NIC architecture

Alex / team — quick technical clarifications and recommendations from the infra side. I kept this focused on storage and node fabric since that was the primary ask.

Storage & CSI recommendations (detailed)
- CSI driver: prefer using the vendor driver that implements inline encryption + snapshot support (e.g., NetLayer CSI v2). If you cannot use vendor CSI, we can accommodate via LUKS + external KMS with our host-attach helper.
- Volume classes:
  * redwood-ephemeral-nvme (localNVMe, fsType=ext4) — for KV cache + temp tensors. Use pod-level emptyDir backed by local PV for fastest throughput.
  * redwood-encrypted-blockstore (RBD/iSCSI with LUKS) — for model artifacts and checkpoints. Recommend 400GB minimum per model shard; configure reclaimPolicy=Retain for snapshots.
  * redwood-archive (object gateway to S3-compatible on-prem) — for cold backup (7–90d).
- Snapshots & backup plan: use VolumeSnapshot + Velero for cross-cluster backups; keep snapshot TTL small (7d) and exports to archive for longer retention.

Node-pool and runtime settings
- Pod sizing: inference pods request 0.5–2 CPU per token-engine, GPU memory requests aligned to model KV cache (we'll provide a sizing table per model).
- Affinity/Taints: dedicate GPU nodes with taints gpu=true:NoSchedule and use tolerations. Use topologySpreadConstraints to avoid rack-level correlated failure.
- Batching: enable our KV-aware batching layer on GPU nodes; this reduces required peak GPUs by ~25% under typical request distributions.

Operational notes
- Upgrade window: schedule control-plane upgrades in a maintenance window with cordon/drain of one master at a time.
- Audit & logs: forward kube-audit to your SIEM (we can supply a pattern set).

I'll attach a short markdown with recommended StorageClass YAML snippets and a PV sizing reference. Happy to walk through during preflight.

Attachments: k8s-storage-profiles-jonas-20261224.md (md)

— Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa / Jonas — this is great and aligns with what our infra team expected. A couple quick replies to the open questions:

1) HSM: we do not need a hardware HSM for root keys at launch; cloud KMS with dual-operator access is acceptable. We may revisit for prod.
2) Snapshot window: nightly 02:00–03:30 local is fine.
3) CSI: NetLayer will manage the vendor CSI; please include their engineer on the preflight.

We approve the proposed node-class split and the encrypted blockstore approach. Please schedule the 90-min preflight for week of Jan 4 — preferred times are Jan 6 (10:00–11:30 PST) or Jan 7 (13:00–14:30 PST). Also, I'm attaching the PO and will sign the order via DocuSign today.

Attachments referenced: PO_HILLSIDE_0192.pdf (attached to the DocuSign envelope)
